# California Water Service Invites Customers to Celebrate 100 Years of Service Dec. 5 in Westlake


November 24, 2026 12:35 pm EST[Download as PDF](https://www.calwatergroup.com/_assets/_68b7494d3a1735c8c3e06fd8f5feeffb/calwatergroup/news/2026-11-24_California_Water_Service_Invites_Customers_to_836.pdf)


THOUSAND OAKS, Calif.— California Water Service (Cal Water) is inviting customers, their families, and community partners to a free customer appreciation celebration as the company marks 100 years of serving California communities.


The family-friendly event will serve as a thank you to customers who have enabled Cal Water to be a part of their lives for generations. Festivities will take place on Saturday, Dec. 5, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Triunfo Canyon Park, located at 980 Aranmoor Ave. in Thousand Oaks.


"Providing safe, clean, reliable water is about much more than infrastructure. It's about supporting the homes, businesses, schools, and communities that depend on us every day," said Mike Jasper, Cal Water's Westlake District Manager. "As we celebrate 100 years of service, we're grateful to our customers for the trust they've placed in us and the opportunity to serve this community for so many decades."


Guests will enjoy complimentary food, soft-serve ice cream, a 65-foot inflatable obstacle course, bounce houses, games, coloring activities, and Cal Water giveaways. Attendees will also be able to adopt a free, drought-tolerant plant while supplies last, learn about water conservation programs and resources available to customers, and enter opportunity drawings for a chance to win a water-efficient washing machine and other prizes.


Founded in 1926 by three World War I veterans, Cal Water has grown from serving four California communities to serving more than 20 districts throughout the state. The company is celebrating its centennial anniversary by thanking customers and highlighting the local teams who deliver safe, clean, reliable water every day.


"For a century, Cal Water has remained committed to serving customers through changing conditions and challenges," Jasper said. "We're proud of our history in the Westlake District and look forward to continuing to invest in the infrastructure, technology, and resources needed to meet our customers' needs for the next 100 years."


Customers are encouraged to RSVP in advance. Those interested in receiving a free drought-tolerant plant must reserve their plant during registration. Food, plants, giveaways, and activities will be available on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last. Opportunity drawing prizes are available to Westlake District customers, who must provide proof of service or residency within the district at check-in to receive drawing tickets.


To learn more about Cal Water's centennial celebration and century of service, visit[100years.calwatergroup.com/events/westlake-district](https://100years.calwatergroup.com/events/westlake-district/) .


**About California Water Service**


California Water Service provides high-quality, reliable water utility services to about 19,500 people through 7,100 service connections in the community of Westlake Village, located in the city of Thousand Oaks, and more than 2.1 million people statewide through 500,000 service connections. Cal Water’s purpose is to enhance the quality of life for customers and communities. Cal Water’s purpose is to enhance the quality of life for customers and communities. To do so, it invests responsibly in water and wastewater infrastructure, sustainability initiatives, and community well-being. The company’s 1,200 employees live by a set of strong core values and share a commitment to protecting the planet, caring for people, and operating with the utmost integrity. The utility, commemorating a century of service this year, has been named one of “America’s Most Responsible Companies” and one of the “World’s Most Trustworthy Companies” by *Newsweek* , a USA Top Workplace, and a Great Place to Work®. More information is available at[www.calwater.com](https://www.calwater.com/) .
